title: Cranberry Juice (Not Fortified, From Concentrate, Shelf Stable)

content.title: About
content.content: Cranberry juice, not fortified with additional vitamins or minerals, is made from cranberry concentrate and packaged as a shelf‑stable product. Cranberries (Vaccinium macrocarpon) are a berry native to northern North America. The juice has a characteristic tart, slightly bitter taste and a bright red color.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Native American tribes traditionally used cranberries to help prevent urinary tract infections.
Juice from concentrate retains most of the aromatic compounds and antioxidants while offering a long, unrefrigerated shelf life.
Cranberries contain proanthocyanidins, which give the fruit its deep red hue.
In the United States, cranberry juice is often served at breakfast alongside oatmeal or granola.
Unsweetened cranberry juice is very low in calories but can be quite acidic.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Cranberries provide proanthocyanidins and vitamin C, which help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports urinary tract health
items.content: Research suggests regular consumption of cranberry juice may reduce the risk of urinary tract infections.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: A non‑fortified, unsweetened product is suitable for calorie‑restricted diets.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: The juice supplies small amounts of B1, B2, and B6, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Cranberry flavonoids may help improve vascular tone and lower blood pressure.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity can irritate the stomach in people with gastritis or ulcer disease.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Cranberry juice can increase the effect of anticoagulants such as warfarin; consult a doctor if you take these medications.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to cranberries.

items.title: Added sugars in some brands
items.content: Although this product is not fortified, some commercial versions may contain added sugars; always check the label.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink the juice on its own, add it to smoothies, use it in sauces for meat, or incorporate it into marinades. It is often diluted with water or apple juice to soften the tartness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the juice in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep it refrigerated and consume within 7‑10 days. Discard the product if the packaging is damaged or the juice develops an off‑odor.
